c.tagline: The Ottoman Empire's second capital, crowned by Sinan's masterpiece mosque.

taxi.fareNote: Yellow taxis are metered ('taksimetre'); confirm the meter is running, as short tourist trips are sometimes negotiated flat-rate instead.

emergency.note: 112 is the unified national emergency number in Türkiye, covering police, ambulance, and fire.

hood_landmark.Karaagac: Lausanne Monument and old Karaagac train station

hood_desc: Edirne's historic core, dominated by Mimar Sinan's UNESCO-listed Selimiye Mosque and the older Uc Serefeli and Eski Camii mosques. Cobbled streets are lined with Ottoman-era shops, tea houses, and the covered bazaar.

A leafy district just across the Meric River, once the terminus of the Orient Express line; the old train station now houses a university fine arts faculty. Riverside parks and the Lausanne Monument make it a peaceful escape from the center.

A residential neighborhood spreading north of the center, mixing everyday apartment blocks with local markets and neighborhood mosques. It offers a glimpse of ordinary Edirne life away from the monuments.

water.note: Locals and visitors alike drink bottled water rather than tap.

transit.map: Edirne Belediyesi municipal bus route maps
transit.note: Edirne's historic core is small and very walkable; dolmus minibuses cover outer neighborhoods and nearby villages.

train: Limited passenger rail; most travelers use intercity buses

tip.r: A small tip of 5-10% in restaurants is appreciated; rounding up taxi fares is common.

food.name: Tava ciger
food.desc: Edirne's signature: paper-thin beef liver floured and flash-fried until crisp, served with fried dried chillies and a raw onion-parsley salad.

places.name: Cicek Tava Ciger Salonu
places.note: Buys local beef liver fresh each morning and slices it to order; a long-running favourite in the bazaar quarter.

places.name: Aydin Tava Ciger
places.note: Well-known liver house out toward Karaagac, praised for fast, professional service and spotless dining rooms.

places.name: Edirne Cigercisi Kemal Usta
places.note: Frying liver for around 35 years; the benchmark plate locals send visitors to try first.

food.name: Edirne badem ezmesi
food.desc: Edirne's famed marzipan: ground almonds and sugar worked into soft, faintly bitter-sweet logs, often tinted and shaped into fruit.

places.name: Kececizade
places.note: Sweet house founded in 1961 whose almond paste is the city's benchmark; boxed for travelling.

places.name: Alipasa Carsisi
places.note: Historic Ottoman arcade lined with confectioners selling almond paste by weight.

places.name: Selimiye Arastasi
places.note: Vaulted 16th-century shopping arcade with sweet stalls handy after visiting the mosque.

food.name: Deva-i misk helvasi
food.desc: An Ottoman 'medicinal' halva of 41 spices bound in sugar and sesame, sold in dark aromatic slabs found almost nowhere else in Turkey.

places.name: Kececizade
places.note: Makes devai misk alongside its almond paste and kavala kurabiyesi; the most reliable source in town.

places.name: Alipasa Carsisi
places.note: Several spice and sweet shops cut it fresh from the block so you can taste before buying.

places.name: Selimiye Arastasi
places.note: Small confectioners here sell gift tins of the spiced halva.

food.name: Kavala kurabiyesi
food.desc: Crumbly almond shortbread carried to Edirne by Balkan settlers, dusted heavily with icing sugar and eaten with tea.

places.name: Kececizade
places.note: The name most associated with kavala kurabiyesi in Edirne; baked daily since 1961.

places.name: Alipasa Carsisi
places.note: Bakery stalls sell them loose by the kilo, still warm in the morning.

food.name: Edirne beyaz peyniri
food.desc: Thrace's prized brined white cheese, firmer and saltier than most, eaten at breakfast with tomato, olives and fresh bread.

places.name: Alipasa Carsisi
places.note: Cheesemongers here cut wheels of Edirne and Kirklareli cheese to order and vacuum-pack for travel.

places.name: Edirne Halk Pazari
places.note: Weekly producers' market where Thracian dairy farmers sell cheese and butter direct.

food.name: Trakya koftesi
food.desc: Thracian grilled meatballs, loosely bound and heavy on cumin, served with piyaz bean salad and grilled green peppers.

places.name: Kofteci Osman
places.note: Central kofte and tava ciger house with quick service and outdoor tables by the old covered market.

places.name: Alipasa Carsisi esnaf lokantalari
places.note: Workaday tradesmen's canteens around the arcade grill kofte to order at lunch prices.

places.name: Saraclar Caddesi grill houses
places.note: The pedestrian main street is lined with ocakbasi grills busy from early evening.

food.name: Hardaliye
food.desc: Thrace's own lightly fermented drink of crushed red grapes steeped with mustard seed and sour cherry leaves; tart, barely alcoholic and deeply local.

places.name: Alipasa Carsisi
places.note: Bottled hardaliye from Thracian producers sold at the arcade's grocers and sweet shops.

places.name: Kececizade
places.note: Stocks bottled hardaliye beside the sweets, convenient for taking home.

places.name: Kofteci Osman
places.note: Serves it chilled by the glass alongside kofte and liver.

food.name: Ayran
food.desc: Salted, whipped yoghurt drink; in Edirne it is the standard, near-obligatory partner to a plate of fried liver.

places.name: Cicek Tava Ciger Salonu
places.note: Serves frothy house ayran in metal cups to cut through the fried liver.

places.name: Kofteci Osman
places.note: Churned ayran poured by the jug with kofte and pide.

landmarks: Selimiye Mosque
Mimar Sinan's self-declared masterpiece, a UNESCO-listed 1575 mosque whose colossal dome and four pencil minarets crown the Ottoman Empire's former capital.
Old Mosque (Eski Cami)
Edirne's oldest imperial mosque, completed in 1414, enchants with nine domes and gigantic calligraphic inscriptions swirling across its pillars.
Üç Şerefeli Mosque
A revolutionary 1447 mosque named for the three-balconied minaret, its bold dome and spiral-patterned minarets bridging Seljuk and classical Ottoman styles.
Complex of Sultan Bayezid II Health Museum
A 1488 Ottoman hospital complex where music and water therapy treated the mentally ill, now an award-winning museum of medical history.
Meriç Bridge
An elegant 13-arch Ottoman stone bridge over the Meriç river, beloved for sunset views and riverside tea gardens south of town.
Karaağaç and the Lausanne Monument
Across the river, this quiet quarter holds the ornate former railway station, Trakya University's museums and the monument marking the 1923 Treaty of Lausanne.
Sarayiçi and the Kırkpınar Arena
On an island of the Tunca stand Justice Tower, remnants of the Ottoman palace and the stadium hosting the ancient Kırkpınar oil-wrestling festival.
Ali Pasha Bazaar (Alipaşa Çarşısı)
A vaulted 16th-century covered market attributed to Sinan, still trading soaps, brooms and Edirne's famous fruit-shaped marzipan along its long stone arcade.
Edirne Grand Synagogue
Reopened in 2015 after restoration, this 1909 Moorish-revival synagogue was once Europe's third largest, testament to Edirne's Sephardic heritage.
Macedonian Tower (Makedonya Kulesi)
A surviving Roman-Byzantine tower of ancient Hadrianopolis' walls, restored with a small exhibition and views over the old town's rooftops.

train.note: No international passenger trains call at Edirne itself - the Istanbul-Sofia and Istanbul-Bucharest sleepers pass through Thrace but use Kapıkule on the border rather than serving the city as a normal stop. Regional trains link Edirne with Kapıkule and Istanbul's Halkalı. Check current TCDD e-bilet listings before assuming a through connection.

intl.op: Nilüfer Turizm and regional carriers — tickets at the Edirne otogar

bus.note: Edirne is only 20 km from the Bulgarian border at Kapıkule and 7 km from the Greek border at Pazarkule, so it is the natural overland gateway between Turkey and the EU. Coaches to Istanbul run roughly hourly and take about 2h30. The Greek crossing at Pazarkule/Kastanies has no public bus - travellers usually take a taxi across. Carry your passport and expect queues at Kapıkule in summer.

ferry.note: Edirne is inland in Thrace on the Meriç and Tunca rivers, neither navigable for passenger services, so there are no ferries.

half.name: Svilengrad
half.blurb: Border town across the Bulgarian frontier with an Ottoman-era stone bridge and a casino strip popular with day-trippers.

half.name: Orestiada
half.blurb: Greek border town on the Evros River, a quick cross-border stop for a change of scenery from Edirne.

full.name: Plovdiv
full.blurb: One of Europe's oldest continuously inhabited cities, with a Roman theater still in use and a restored old town.

full.name: Istanbul
full.blurb: Turkey's largest city straddling Europe and Asia, with the Hagia Sophia, Blue Mosque, and Grand Bazaar.
